name: r9-vectors-signer-report
note: A native manager's signed report of its control-record signing journal (host-work-v1 §11.1 "The signer report"; Astation #114 item 4, agreed with Astation, #114 comment 7089435073), for a Station recovering from a rollback; version 2, its process roster (option (i), agreed with Astation, #114 comment 7208700195): wire {"body":{…},"sig"}, the body {type: atem-signer-report, v: 2, account_id, genesis_hash, head{seq, hash}, signer, slot, process, challenge{origin, connection, nonce, issued_at, expires_at}, recovery{generation, plan_id, candidate_feed_id, source_hash, evidence_hash}, journal{id, since, revision, records, records_hash, drafts, drafts_hash, processes, processes_hash}} signed by a current native member's own auth_key (signer member:<device_id>; one that held manage at some seq of the list) over enc(["atem-signer-report-v2", jcs(body)]) (R9.1), under the alg the device list pins. v1 (v 1, its journal without processes, under atem-signer-report-v1) is refused as malformed everywhere: no compatibility path. A challenge is what the minter stores, {signer, slot, origin, connection, nonce, issued_at, expires_at, recovery}: signer member:<id>, slot and ids 1-128 bytes of [A-Za-z0-9._:-], origin exact as station_route::normalize_relay writes it, connection 1 to 2^53-1, nonce 32 bytes, process and journal.id 16 bytes (base64url, no padding), 0 < expires_at - issued_at <= 30000 ms, recovery.generation a canonical decimal string 1 to 2^63-1 (no sign, no leading zero), plan_id and candidate_feed_id UUID v4, the hashes lowercase hex SHA-256; journal.since 1 to 2^53-1, revision, records and drafts 0 to 2^53-1, processes 1 to 2^53-1; a challenge text is at most 4,096 bytes, the body's jcs at most 4,096 bytes and the object at most 16 KiB; no null, no array, no kit_sig, no field beyond these at any level, no duplicate key (escaped ones included). The plan's records (B2): a control-record body (r9-vectors-host-work-control's form) this member signs (signer member:<id>), of this account and genesis, a service's revoke or interrupt_running naming the challenge's origin, or a host principal's interrupt_running (no origin). records_hash = SHA-256(enc(["atem-signer-report-records-v1", d1…dn])) over each record body's SHA-256(jcs(body)) (32 bytes), sorted by bytes; drafts_hash the same with "atem-signer-report-drafts-v1". The process roster: the adapter durably appends attach{process} the first time a process takes the journal's lock, before that process can append any signing entry (B6); processes counts the process generations attached to the journal and processes_hash = SHA-256(enc(["atem-signer-report-processes-v1", p1…pn])) over their 16 raw bytes each (the body's process form), sorted by bytes; a roster holds at most 4,096 ids (Atem's reading: nothing else a report carries is bounded as a list). Device lists: log L of r9-vectors-membership-log followed by `chain` (labels of `entries`), then the carriage `freeze` (a label of r9-vectors-membership-log's others) when a case names one, which freezes it; each list verified at the case's now_ms. Keys are r9-vectors-keys' (`signed_with` names <name>/<part>: auth, host_key, or recovery/sign for the kit's recovery key); dev-desk is the Ed25519 native the chain adds without manage (SR7_add_desk) and makes a manager (SR8_desk_manages). `records`: the control records the cases use, each body, its jcs and digest, and the record as its signer signed it. `challenges`: texts read by SignerReportChallenge::parse (bindings parse_signer_report_challenge): `fields` when read, else `code`. `valid` and `invalid`: verify_signer_report(list, report, the stored challenge `challenge`, the exported signed records `exported`, the exported roster `exported_processes` (base64url ids), now_ms): `expect` is the VerifiedSignerReport (process base64url, at_head true at the list's head, false at an ancestor, journal.id base64url, records the verified records as given, processes the verified roster sorted by bytes, base64url), or `code`, the first failure in the order malformed, frozen, wrong_account, unknown_signer, not_a_manager, bad_signature, stale_log, fork, signer_mismatch, slot_mismatch, challenge_mismatch, recovery_mismatch, records_mismatch, processes_mismatch, expired (bindings: Report{code}). processes_mismatch is an exported roster that isn't exactly the report's processes: a malformed id (not 16 bytes of base64url), a duplicate, another count or processes_hash than the report's, or a roster without the report's own process. What a verified roster proves: the signer attested that these processes attached to journal id, the adapter's word under B6, exactly as strong as records; never evidence about a process absent from the set, nor about another journal. The resolution rule: a displaced process P of member M is accounted for by a verified report R iff R's signer is M and P is in R's processes; comparing journals and generations is the Station's. records_mismatch is an exported record that isn't a signed control record of the plan by this member, one whose signature doesn't verify under its key (low S), a duplicate, or another count or records_hash than the report's: a body in signing with no saved signature is in records and can't be exported, so such a report is refused (Astation's conservative rule). A report's process is the fixed bytes "vectors-process!", its roster's other ids "earlier-process!" and "a-later-process!"; a builder draws its own once per loaded core (process_generation). `builder`: signer_report_body(list, challenge, signer, slot, station, journal{id, since, revision, records, drafts: the bodies' texts, processes: the roster's ids but the reporter's own}, now_ms), the runner adding its own process_generation (bindings verifier_report_process) to journal.processes, after them, when `own_process` is true: `body_but_process` (the body it builds, but its process and its journal.processes_hash, which covers the process: both the loaded core's own; the runner checks processes_hash over journal.processes and its own), or `code` (origin_mismatch when the challenge's origin isn't station normalized; malformed for a journal body that isn't one of the plan's records by this member, one twice in a set, or a roster without the reporter's own process, with an id twice or out of its grammar). `request`: the immutable request (bindings SignerReportRequest): built as a builder case, its sign_request (`purpose`, `fresh_confirmation`, `label`; input = enc([label, jcs(body)]), body_json = jcs(body)), then each `finishes` entry signs with `signed_with` the input of the held body (`over: held`) or of a request for the same challenge and journal with another `slot` (`over: {slot}`), and finish gives the report, byte-equal to {"body":<held body>,"sig":<the signature, low S>}, or `code`. `plan_predicate` (Astation's ask, #114 comment 7093796254): signer_report_plan_record(list, body, member, origin) (bindings signer_report_plan_record): whether a control-record body is one of the plan's records for member (member:<id>) at origin (the challenge's, exactly as normalize_relay writes it), the account and genesis the list's (L + `chain`, then `freeze`): `in_plan` true, or false with `reason`, in the order checked another_account, another_genesis, another_signer (another member, or the principal's own key), then another_origin (a service's revoke or interrupt_running naming another origin), or `code` malformed (this member's cover, hold or release, judged after the signer and before the origin; a body that isn't a control record's, read as the builder reads a journal's; a member that isn't member:<id>; an origin not in its exact form). The builder reads a journal's bodies by this one rule: a body in the plan is one it takes in a set, anything else refuses the build. Bodies only: the list's freeze and the member's standing change no answer. Which bodies are in the plan is the agreed B2 rule with agreed reading (c); its three readings are agreed with Astation (Astation #114 comment 7209301522): another account, genesis or signer not in the plan with a reason (never malformed), the order account, genesis, signer, action, origin, and the four reason codes. Consistency only: never completeness of anything outside the journal. Atem's readings, agreed with Astation, #114 comment 7093796254 (the agreed text left them open; each is fail-closed): (a) a challenge's signer is member:<id> only, a service: one malformed when read (a report body naming a service, a host, a grant or recovery is unknown_signer, as agreed); (b) the builder also takes now_ms and refuses an expired challenge; (c) a service's records of the plan are its revoke and interrupt_running only, so this member's cover, hold or release body refuses the build (malformed), never skipped; (d) one body may be both a record and a draft (only a body twice in one set is refused); (e) journal.since is compared with nothing, head.seq included.
